meta.description: Sends rate requests to partners from a Gmail account and records the thread id against each request, so replies can be matched back. Same Gmail credential as workflow 04 — authorise once, used by both.

nodes.name: Send RFQ for an enquiry
nodes.notes: POST { "ref": "ARX-ENQ-9001" }. Called from the CRM, or by hand during a demo.

nodes.name: SHIPMATE picks the partners
nodes.notes: Ranks on tags, then on what memory says each partner actually does, then gates on role — a CHA cannot quote ocean freight however well its tags match. Records one request per partner and creates a commitment per partner so the sentinel chases the quiet ones.

nodes.name: Anyone to ask?
nodes.notes: No eligible partner is a real outcome, not an error — the burst says why, and the desk needs to see that rather than a silent nothing.

nodes.name: Send the rate request
nodes.notes: Plain text on purpose. A partner's mail client quotes plain text cleanly on reply, which keeps the thread readable — and the thread is how the answer gets matched back.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ partnerEmail: $('One mail per partner').item.json.to, threadRef: $json.threadId }) }}

nodes.name: Record the thread id
nodes.notes: Goes through SHIPMATE rather than PATCHing Postgres directly. The alternative was putting the service_role key into this workflow, and that key bypasses RLS on every table in the CRM — it belongs in one process, not in a JSON that gets exported and shared. Gmail returns threadId on send; it is the only durable link between a request and its answer.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ref: $('SHIPMATE picks the partners').item.json.body.ref, asked: $('SHIPMATE picks the partners').item.json.body.recipients.length, why: $('SHIPMATE picks the partners').item.json.body.why }) }}

parameters.content:
## Collecting the replies

Workflow **04** already polls this mailbox. A partner's reply arrives there like any other mail — what makes it an RFQ reply is that its `threadId` matches a row in `partner_quotes`.

So 04's branch for it is:

`POST {{ $env.SHIPMATE_BASE }}/rfq/collect`
with `{ threadRef: <threadId>, text: <body> }`

If the thread matches nothing outstanding, SHIPMATE says so and the mail falls through to the ordinary enquiry reader. Nothing is guessed at.
